prompt:
Make this custom dropdown accessible. It's currently a div-based menu with no keyboard support: ```html
Options
Option A
Option B
```
assertions: Output adds an appropriate role (e.g. button/menu/menuitem) to the interactive divs
Output adds tabindex="0" to the toggle and items so they're keyboard-reachable
Output adds a descriptive aria-label or accessible name to the toggle
Output adds keydown handling for Space/Enter on the custom controls, not just onclick
Output does not rely on click-only interaction for any of the custom controls
Output adds role="status" or aria-busy to the loading state
Output adds role="alert" to the error banner
Output uses a visually-hidden aria-live="polite" region (with aria-atomic if appropriate) for dynamic status text that isn't already covered by role=alert/status
Output does not leave the loading/error state changes silent to assistive tech
Output checks prefers-reduced-motion before initiating the fetch call, not just before calling play/autoplay
Output skips the network request entirely when reduced motion is preferred, rather than fetching the JSON and only suppressing playback
Output still renders a reasonable non-animated fallback or nothing, rather than a broken/missing element
Output does not fetch the animation data unconditionally regardless of the media query
Output moves focus programmatically to the results heading/landmark after results appear
Output adds tabindex="-1" to the target heading/landmark so it's focusable without being in the natural tab order
Output calls .focus() on that element via a ref after the content renders
Output does not attempt to call .focus() directly on non-focusable content without the tabindex="-1" addition
